corrections: Normalized untrusted trace identifiers before logging.
Applied a nonce-based CSP and blocked external dashboard assets.
Pinned GitHub Actions and container bases to immutable commit or image digests.
Verified the final tree and image with Gitleaks, pip-audit, and Trivy.
evidence_commands: docker run ... trivy image --severity HIGH,CRITICAL mezo-ai-control-plane:local

findings.evidence: Attacker-controlled unmatched paths were initially usable as request metric labels.
findings.fix: Metrics now use matched route templates and collapse all unmatched paths to __unmatched__.
findings.risk: Unbounded label cardinality could grow process memory and degrade the API.

findings.evidence: The first dashboard draft persisted the API key in sessionStorage.
findings.fix: The key is held only in page memory and is cleared on reload or tab close.
findings.risk: A browser-side persistence mechanism unnecessarily extended credential lifetime.

findings.evidence: A literal placeholder API key in a curl example triggered the secret scanner.
findings.fix: The example now reads the value from CONTROL_PLANE_API_KEY.
findings.risk: Examples that resemble credentials reduce signal quality in secret scanning.

receipts.revisit: Any authentication, browser storage, logging, metrics-label, workflow, or dependency-source change

corrections: Kept dashboard, metrics, alert evaluation, reports, tracing, evidence, and evals in explicit modules.
Preserved existing application service and repository boundaries instead of adding database access to the dashboard.

findings.evidence: The worker path originally wrote EvidenceRow directly while the application path wrote both EvidenceRow and the hash ledger.
findings.fix: Both paths now call one transactional append_evidence_records boundary.
findings.risk: Two persistence paths could diverge and make worker evidence unverifiable.

findings.evidence: Provider, repeated-failure, and cost rules existed before their cross-process publishers were connected.
findings.fix: Unpublished metrics are explicitly returned as unavailable and cannot fire or appear healthy.
findings.risk: Substituting zero would falsely imply those signals had been measured.

receipts.revisit: When provider and cost publishers are connected across worker and API processes

corrections: Added typed task report, observability snapshot, alert, and Prometheus contracts.
Added contract tests for content types, authentication, CSP, report digest, unavailable metrics, and bounded unmatched-route labels.

findings.evidence: A missing signal must be distinguishable from a measured zero value.
findings.fix: Alert evaluations include available, nullable value, and unavailable_metrics at the API boundary.
findings.risk: Operators could interpret unavailable telemetry as a healthy measurement.

receipts.revisit: Any route, response schema, authentication exemption, or dashboard action change

corrections: Separated deterministic evaluation contracts, fixtures, runner, and CLI.
Kept verification scripts small and fail-closed.
Removed placeholder telemetry values instead of adding comments around false defaults.

findings.evidence: Duplicating ledger construction in repositories and workers would couple schema details to multiple callers.
findings.fix: Canonical ledger writes live in evidence_writer.py and callers supply only validated EvidenceItem data.
findings.risk: Future evidence changes could update one caller but not the other.

receipts.revisit: When evidence or alert modules gain additional persistence or transport adapters

corrections: Added adversarial tests for label cardinality, trace redaction, ledger tampering, mixed task IDs, unavailable signals, and database URL normalization.
Added migration upgrade/downgrade assertions for evidence_ledger.
Final real-infrastructure result: 126 passed. Final eval result: 11/11 passed.
evidence_commands: DATABASE_URL=postgres://... uv run alembic upgrade head

findings.evidence: The isolated suite passed while the real PostgreSQL/Redis flow exposed an empty evidence ledger for worker-written evidence.
findings.fix: Added ledger assertions to the real worker flow and reran every test against pinned PostgreSQL and Redis containers.
findings.risk: Mock-only confidence would have shipped an integrity gap.

receipts.revisit: When worker persistence, migrations, alert rules, or dashboard controls change

corrections: Added task-local unique sequence and globally unique entry hash constraints.
Verified one migration head and a real upgrade to 0003_evidence_ledger.
Kept automatic schema downgrade out of the deployment workflow.
evidence_commands: DATABASE_URL=postgres://... uv run alembic upgrade head

findings.evidence: Worker evidence bypassed the ledger until tested with the real database.
findings.fix: Task-row locking and one transaction now cover the compatibility row and hash-chain entry for all durable writers.
findings.risk: A completed task could contain compatibility evidence without an integrity chain.

findings.evidence: Fly/Postgres may provide postgres:// or postgresql:// while runtime and migrations require different SQLAlchemy drivers.
findings.fix: Central URL normalization maps common forms to asyncpg for runtime and psycopg for Alembic without logging credentials.
findings.risk: A release migration could fail before deployment despite a valid managed database URL.

receipts.revisit: Before any destructive migration or evidence schema change

corrections: Release migrations run before rolling replacement and readiness gates machine health.
Final image runs as UID 10001 and passed a read-only, no-network, capability-dropped smoke test.
Authenticated post-deploy checks cover task reads, alerts, and metrics.
No production deployment or production migration was executed.

findings.evidence: The initial manual deployment workflow could be dispatched from a non-main ref.
findings.fix: The job now requires refs/heads/main, exact DEPLOY confirmation, and the protected production environment.
findings.risk: An approved environment run could deploy code that had not been merged to the protected branch.

findings.evidence: An unpinned base and isolated build dependency resolution would weaken reproducibility.
findings.fix: Base images, build dependencies, runtime dependencies, Compose services, and workflow actions are pinned.
findings.risk: Identical source could produce different runtime contents over time.

receipts.revisit: Before the first production deployment and whenever Fly topology or release commands change

corrections: Documented dashboard credential handling, evidence integrity, alerts, evals, deployment, rollback, and incident runbooks.
Final readiness explicitly records that no production deployment, migration, or merge was performed.

findings.evidence: Documentation initially described unconnected alert inputs as zero-valued.
findings.fix: Documentation and API now identify those metrics as unavailable until publishers exist.
findings.risk: Operators could infer measurement coverage that did not exist.

receipts.revisit: Whenever operational behavior, approval boundaries, or production procedures change

corrections: Added 11 safe and adversarial fixtures with expected accept/reject outcomes.
CI fails if any unsafe fixture is accepted or any known-safe fixture is rejected.
No eval fixture can trigger a real tool, merge, deployment, migration, or credential change.

findings.evidence: Success claims, tool names, reviewer identity, corrective rounds, protected branches, and approval-requiring actions need deterministic acceptance checks outside model prose.
findings.fix: The eval boundary rejects ungrounded root cause claims, unknown tools, prompt injection, self-review, unbounded loops, failed tests, protected-branch writes, and missing approvals.
findings.risk: A fluent model response could claim completion or authorize an unsafe action without evidence.

receipts.revisit: Whenever agent roles, tools, approval actions, reviewer policy, or completion criteria change
